name: Edwin VanCleef
summary: In the Deadmines, brilliant Edwin VanCleef commands the Defias Brotherhood. He once led the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. The House of Nobles denied the workers their promised pay, and VanCleef now seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore.

sections.title: Architect of the Kingdom
sections.body: Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild as it rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War. A peerless craftsman and idealist, he mastered architecture and directed the building of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. His childhood friend Mathias Shaw trained him in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft, making VanCleef a deadly operative as well as a master architect.

sections.title: The Riot and the Brotherhood
sections.body: After years of labor, the Stonemasons finished rebuilding Stormwind. The House of Nobles had run up colossal debts through military campaigns and refused the guild its promised compensation. VanCleef demanded restitution, but the nobles dissolved the guild. He led the workers in a riot and out of the city. In the chaos, his lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and left in the Stockade. In Westfall, VanCleef gathered the exiled workers and allied outcasts under the Defias Brotherhood's banner.

sections.title: Retribution from the Shadows
sections.body: The Defias drove Westfall's farmers from their homes and claimed its rich gold deposits while the crown neglected the countryside. Deep in Moonbrook's Deadmines, VanCleef directs the building of a massive juggernaut warship for an armed assault on Stormwind. The House of Nobles dismisses the thieves as disorganized brigands, while VanCleef has joined forces with river crooks, gnolls, and pirates. His embittered labor union has become an army poised against the monarchy.

faq.answer: Edwin VanCleef leads the Defias Brotherhood and once served as Guildmaster of the Stonemasons. He is the master architect who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Horde destroyed it during the First War.

faq.q: Why did the Stonemasons revolt against Stormwind?
faq.answer: After the Stonemasons rebuilt Stormwind City, the House of Nobles refused to pay the guild its agreed wages because the kingdom was deeply in debt. VanCleef and the workers protested, but the nobles disbanded the guild, and violent riots broke out in the streets.
Edwin VanCleef commands the Defias Brotherhood from the innermost sanctum of the Deadmines in Westfall. The entrance is rumored to lie through the quiet village of Moonbrook.

faq.q: What is his connection to Mathias Shaw?
faq.answer: Mathias Shaw was Edwin VanCleef's childhood friend. Shaw trained VanCleef in stealth, thievery, and combat, hoping he would join the royal intelligence agency SI:7.

faq.q: What happened to Bazil Thredd during the riot?
faq.answer: During the riots, VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and held in prison. While VanCleef led the Stonemasons out of the city, Thredd was all but forgotten in the Stockade as he awaited trial and questioning.

faq.q: What is he building in the Deadmines?
faq.answer: The Defias have conscripted clever goblins to help build something terrible at the bottom of the Deadmines, but what it may be remains uncertain.

angles.text: For humans of Stormwind, VanCleef's story shows the cost of the kingdom's postwar recovery: a loyal hero whose own livelihood was denied, turning him into the realm's deadliest insurgent.
Mathias Shaw, the leader of SI:7, trained VanCleef himself. VanCleef became one of Azeroth's most capable rogues, combining guild leadership with elite assassination techniques.
Alliance commanders see VanCleef as the leading internal security threat to southern human lands. His actions paralyze Westfall and the borders of Elwynn Forest.
